code:
R-TYPE (Rainbow Arts 1988, Manfred Trenz) - 1:1 port of the main program
Every byte of $0812-$A133 is the original. Code blocks sit at their original
addresses, so labels are for reading - nothing is relocated.

MAIN IMAGE (this workspace = BOOT on the D64)
$0812-$636F  game engine (scrolling, sprites, collisions, weapons, IRQs)
$6200        LEVEL_LOAD - KERNAL loads "+" then 3 level files by name
$6370-$85CA  title / intro sequence + intro music player ($6800)
$85CB        RT_INTRO_FONT   copied to $C000 by INTRO_START
$8B63        RT_HUD_SCREEN   copied to $CEF8 (bottom HUD rows)
$8C53        RT_HUD_CHARS    copied to $C600 (chars 192-255)
$8E53        RT_SPRITES      copied to $D000 (pointers $40-$7B)
$9D53        RT_GAME_FONT    copied to $C800 (also sprites $7C-$7F)
VIC bank 3: screen $CC00, charsets $C000 / $C800 / $E000

DISK FILES (LOAD_ORG RT_DISK, all DISK ONLY - the game loads them itself)
+  $CD00  level unpacker ($CE60)
A D G J M P S V   $6370  level code / map / music (over the title area)
B E H K N Q T W   $86AC  level charset + data
C F I L O R U X   $E000  level graphics (bank 3)
Y  $6800  end sequence
Level files stay packed (P and V never were): unpacked they need ~685
blocks, more than a D64 holds. Build target must be D64.

code:
HOW IT STARTS
SYSTEM INIT is just JMP $8000 (the crack's own entry). INTRO_START plays the
Rainbow Arts intro; F1 then FIRE (port 1) goes to GAME_INIT ($0815), which
unpacks the graphics (GFX_UNPACK $1794) and calls LEVEL_LOAD.

EDITING
Sprites, HUD chars and fonts are normal assets - edit them and rebuild.
Code: edit the blocks freely but keep each one ending where it started
(.pc jumps mark left-out zero runs). Instructions shown as .byte are ones the
Dev Machine assembler would encode differently (absolute $00xx etc) - the
comment says what they are.

Labels are auto-named from what each routine touches (READ_JOY,
SPRITE_MOVE, IRQ_HANDLER...); a number means several do the same job.
